rationale: Hapax in this passage; context demands a verb of exposure/beholding parallel to ⲛⲉⲩ ⲁⲣⲁⲥ 'see her' and ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ 'reveal.' Etymology unidentified — possibly a Lyc reflex of an exposure-verb. Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

Compound ⲕⲉ- ('other') + ⲃⲁⲩⲟⲛⲉ (unidentified). Listed alongside ⲣⲙⲙⲏⲉ 'men of truth' and ⲉⲩⲧⲉⲛⲏⲥ 'noble ones' as a third social class. Possibly Greek-derived from βάναυσοι 'mechanics, common artisans' or a related class-term. Confidence low.
Lyc reflex of ⲗⲁϩ 'occasion, time, circumstance' (Sah ⲣⲁⲁⲩ/ⲣⲁⲩⲉ). Used in the phrase ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲗⲁⲁⲉⲍ 'in some occasion,' fitting standard Coptic idiom for 'on a particular occasion.'
Demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲧⲁⲛⲧⲛ̄ (= ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲛ 'be like, comparison'). Standard exegetical introducer for parable-application: 'according to this comparison.' Same root as ⲥⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲛⲧ 'be likened' in glossary.

proposed_english: the Most High / the Lofty One
rationale: Substantival relative ⲡⲉⲧ- ('the one who') + ⲭⲁⲥⲉ ('be high, lofty,' Lyc qualitative of ϫⲓⲥⲉ). Already attested in glossary as element of ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲟ ⲉⲧⲭⲁⲥⲉ 'the lofty kingship.' Here functions as divine title for the Third Ambassador / the Most High in whose image Adam and Eve were fashioned.
Verbal idiom ⲣ̄- ('do, make') + ⲡⲙⲉⲉⲩⲉ ('the thought/memory'). Standard Coptic for 'make memorial of,' fits cultic-mnemonic context (ποιεῖν εἰς ἀνάμνησιν).
Lyc 2pl object suffix ⲗⲉⲧ-/ⲧⲏⲛⲉ in causative ⲁⲓ̈ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲗⲉⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ 'I have raised you up.' The ⲗ-form may reflect the Lycopolitan dative pronoun assimilated into the verb. Confidence moderate.
